beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Deepa Shenoy, and this video is about how AI can sound confident and still be wrong. This is Liam, narrating for Deepa.

shot.visual_intent: HAI opening with Deepa, exact supplied title, @HumanitariansAI, and the explicit Liam-for-Deepa disclosure. The composer UI is illustrative, not a real captured session.

show.event: HAI opening with Deepa, exact supplied title, @HumanitariansAI, and the explicit Liam-for-Deepa disclosure. The composer UI is illustrative, not a real captured session.

props.command: Explain how AI can sound confident and still be wrong.

beats.narration_text: A language model can give a convincing answer without checking every claim. Let’s see why plausible wording and verified facts are different. That is the gap.

shot.visual_intent: Mandatory overview: show the initial assumption “A confident answer has been checked” revised to “A confident answer still needs checking.” HAI palette; 0.8-second lead silence; measured window must meet the skill minimum.

show.event: Mandatory overview: show the initial assumption “A confident answer has been checked” revised to “A confident answer still needs checking.” HAI palette; 0.8-second lead silence; measured window must meet the skill minimum.

props.text:
A confident answer
has been checked.
Wait, has it?
A confident answer

qc.sparse_reason: Mandatory hesitant-writer overview accumulates, revises and lands the film’s central frame.

beats.narration_text: An AI hallucination is a fluent answer that includes false or unsupported information.

shot.visual_intent: Definition card: “fluent answer” paired with “false or unsupported claim.” Keep the term plain and avoid implying all generative content is intended as fact.

show.event: Definition card: “fluent answer” paired with “false or unsupported claim.” Keep the term plain and avoid implying all generative content is intended as fact.

props.command: Define an AI hallucination as a fluent answer that contains false or unsupported information.

beats.narration_text: A language model predicts tokens from patterns learned during training. That can produce useful text, but ordinary generation does not automatically check each new claim against a trusted source.

shot.visual_intent: Conceptual token-by-token pattern illustration; show a separate trusted-source check as absent unless a tool is added. This is an explanatory diagram, not a literal model trace.

show.event: Conceptual token-by-token pattern illustration; show a separate trusted-source check as absent unless a tool is added. This is an explanatory diagram, not a literal model trace.

beats.narration_text: Fictional example: imagine a made-up country called Bellora. Asked for its capital, an AI confidently answers, “Lumen.” Both names are invented; a confident sentence is not evidence.

shot.visual_intent: Prominent “FICTIONAL EXAMPLE” card. Bellora and Lumen both labeled “made up”; do not depict an actual map or present it as a real model output.

show.event: Prominent “FICTIONAL EXAMPLE” card. Bellora and Lumen both labeled “made up”; do not depict an actual map or present it as a real model output.

props.command: Create a clearly fictional example of a confident answer that has no verified evidence.
output: Label every invented name as fictional
Do not show it as a real model result

beats.narration_text: That matters when people rely on invented citations, instructions, or details in consequential decisions.

shot.visual_intent: Risk pathway: confident false answer → reliance → possible decision error. Mark as a possible risk, not a frequency or prediction.

show.event: Risk pathway: confident false answer → reliance → possible decision error. Mark as a possible risk, not a frequency or prediction.

beats.narration_text: Check important claims against reliable sources. Give useful context. Retrieval can bring relevant documents into an answer when appropriate. These steps reduce risk; they cannot guarantee truth.

shot.visual_intent: Four practical actions: verify; check reliable sources; provide context; use retrieval/grounding when appropriate. End with the explicit limit “helps, not a guarantee.”

show.event: Four practical actions: verify; check reliable sources; provide context; use retrieval/grounding when appropriate. End with the explicit limit “helps, not a guarantee.”

props.command: Show practical ways to check important AI claims and explain why these steps are not guarantees.

beats.narration_text: Remember: plausible is not verified. Treat important claims as questions to check.

shot.visual_intent: Verdict artifact: “Plausible ≠ verified” and “Check consequential claims.” Use HAI palette/brand label rather than the source scene’s default channel branding.

show.event: Verdict artifact: “Plausible ≠ verified” and “Check consequential claims.” Use HAI palette/brand label rather than the source scene’s default channel branding.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Ask Claude: “Using only these sources I paste, answer my question and cite each claim to a passage. Mark unsupported claims.” Remove one source and compare. Run it on your own question and sources.

shot.visual_intent: Second-to-last HAI RESEARCH exercise. Show the paste-ready prompt as an exercise, not as a completed real session. Pair claims with cited passages and an unsupported marker; do not fabricate output.

show.event: Second-to-last HAI RESEARCH exercise. Show the paste-ready prompt as an exercise, not as a completed real session. Pair claims with cited passages and an unsupported marker; do not fabricate output.

props.command: Use only my pasted sources. Cite each claim to a passage. Mark unsupported claims.

cli_exercise.ask: claude "Using only the source passages I paste below, answer my question. Cite every factual claim to a passage, and mark anything the passages do not support."
cli_exercise.output_description: A short answer with claim-level source passages and unsupported claims clearly marked.
cli_exercise.change: Remove one source passage and run the same question again.
cli_exercise.output2_description: A comparison showing which claims lost support, changed, or remain supported by the remaining passages.
cli_exercise.next_step: Run it on your own question and sources.
